summary.whatChanges: Adds `.validate()` and `.validateAsync()` instance methods to classic Zod schemas, delegating to the existing top-level parse helpers. `.validate()` acts as a type guard on the schema's input type. Docs now show the method form, noting `z.validate(schema, data)` remains the zod/mini form. Tests cover narrowing, params, async, and mini's absence of the methods.
behaviorChanges: Classic schemas expose `.validate(data, params?)` returning a boolean that narrows `data` to the schema's input type
Classic schemas expose `.validateAsync(data, params?)` returning a Promise<boolean> for async refinements
Calling `.validate()` on a schema with async refinements throws `$ZodAsyncError`
zod/mini schemas still have no validate methods; only the top-level `z.validate()` function
Docs recommend `.validate()`/`.validateAsync()` methods over the top-level function for classic Zod
risks: New `validate`/`validateAsync` method names could collide with user-defined properties or subclass members on ZodType
Tests note that passing a `params` context bypasses the compiled fast path, so `.validate()` with params on a compiled schema is slower than the documented fast path
